_comment: Shared cases for how the sessions table groups (#546, #619).
Grouping stays client-side because the mode is what the operator chose, and
sending every choice to the daemon for a read-only board buys nothing (ADR-0011).
internal/tui/group_shared_test.go and test/js/dashboard.test.mjs read this file.
The `modes` list replaces a regex scrape: a Go test used to pull the GROUP_MODES
array out of lib.js with a regular expression. That checked a constant matched
and could say nothing about behaviour at a boundary, which is where the rules in
this repository have actually diverged. It retired `jsArrayFromFile`; #633
retired its last clone, so no Go test reads a JavaScript constant by regex.

keys.why: project groups on the daemon's `project`, so two machines that checked the same project out under different roots meet in one group (#618)
the same project under another root lands on the same key
a session with no directory carries the daemon's dash and groups under it rather than under an empty key
an unnamed machine gives an empty key rather than a missing one
with grouping off there is one group and no header, and the key falls back to the machine rather than to nothing
